{{Quote|I ain't no rodent! I'm more what ya call yer basic Lepus carnivorus&mdash;a meat eatin', rocket ridin' rabbit ta you, junior!|Jaxxon, rebuking [[Warto]]|<ref name="M8">[[Star Wars (1977) 8|''Star Wars'' (1977) 8]]</ref>}}
The '''Lepi''', also known as the '''Lepus carnivorus''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Rabbit/Legends|rabbit]] ranging in [[Color/Legends|color]] from green to dark blue. Their most distinctive features were long [[Ear/Legends|ears]] and [[Foot/Legends|feet]] and buck [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. Native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coachelle Prime/Legends|Coachelle Prime]], their high [[Reproduction/Legends|reproductive]] rate forced them to colonize the entire [[Star system/Legends|star system]] to avoid overcrowding. The Lepus carnivorus were typically gregarious individuals, although prone to bursts of anger if their family or species was insulted. Lepi were constantly in motion and were known for their speed.

The most famous Lepus carnivorus was the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Jaxxon/Legends|Jaxxon]], best known for his part in defending a [[City/Legends|village]] on [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]], alongside [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] hero [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. Along with six others, they repelled the superior forces of the [[Cloud-Riders/Legends|Cloud-Riders]]. Other notable Lepi included the criminal [[Grubbat Fhilch]], executed by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], and the [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] colonist [[Heff (Lepi)|Heff]], killed by [[Jodo Kast]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Y'know how us rocket rabbit types are: we just can't stand still.|Jaxxon|<ref name="M10">[[Star Wars (1977) 10|''Star Wars'' (1977) 10]]</ref>}}
[[File:Grubbat_Fhilch.jpg|thumb|left|upright|A long-tailed Lepi]]
The Lepus carnivorus<ref name="M8" /> were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] bipedal [[Rabbit/Legends|lagomorphs]] with large [[Ear/Legends|ears]] and [[Foot/Legends|feet]]. They had lanky frames, with [[Gender/Legends|males]] averaging 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height, while the smaller females averaged 1.6 meters. The strong [[Limb/Legends|legs]] of the Lepi were capable of great speeds as well as delivering powerful kicks, often used in fights to bludgeon their opponents. Lepi were covered in short [[Hair/Legends|fur]] that ranged in [[Color/Legends|color]] from green to dark blue<ref name="UAA" /> to white.<ref name="TM" /> Lepi also had tails, although these differed in length from stubby to quite long.<ref name="Fortune" />

The Lepus carnivorus had large [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]&mdash;likely adapted for dark warrens&mdash;which gave them sharp vision. That occasionally led to the misconception that Lepi consumed [[Carrot/Legends|space carrots]], which were known to improve eyesight. However, most Lepi preferred various forms of meat, such as [[hambones]]. Some Lepi even claimed to be [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]].<ref name="M10" /> A number of long whiskers grew from their short snouts. Long [[Tooth/Legends|incisors]], occasionally referred to as "buck teeth," jutted from their jaws, useful in their omnivorous diets.<ref name="NB1" /> The long ears of the Lepi were very sensitive and occasionally colored in different shades, such as pink fur.<ref name="TM" />

The Lepus carnivorus had a very high metabolism such that they were virtually always in motion, giving them an appearance of flightiness. That skittishness was also influenced by their evolution from high-strung herbivores; their "fight-or-flight" instinct very much favored flight.<ref name="GMR">{{GamerCite|4|The Starhoppers of Aduba-3}}</ref>

Lepus carnivorus sexually matured around age ten, when they were considered young adults. Females gave [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] in prodigious numbers; mothers often had up to three dozen offspring in their lifespan. Lepi reached old age around sixty to seventy-four, after which they were considered venerable.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Never send a man out to do a rabbit's job.|Jaxxon|<ref name="M10" />}}
Lepus carnivorus society revolved around the vast warrens they built under the surface of their [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. Larger families lived in their own smaller burrows. Lepi were fiercely loyal and proud of their families. They were quick to anger and prone to violence, especially in reaction to insults to their family or [[Species/Legends|species]]. Their awkward appearance subjected them to mockery. However, as a whole, Lepi were typically a gregarious species, quick witted with a strong sense of humor.<ref name="GMR" />

[[File:Lepi2.jpg|thumb|right|upright|A Lepi]]
The Lepi were often curious and impulsive, leading many to seek out adventure far from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]]. That also stemmed from a desire to rise above the insults they often received. It was common among Lepi to find a determination to achieve great deeds not only for personal fame, but also to redeem their species in the eyes of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="GMR" />

The native language, both written and oral, of the Lepi was [[Lepese]], or Lepp. However, that quickly became secondary to [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] as the language of preference.<ref name="GMR" /> Non-Lepi, such as [[Seeqov Thranx]], a [[Vratix/Legends|Vratix]] research [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], were capable of learning the language.<ref name="PH">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031113thyferra2|series=Thyferra: Bacta Basics|text=Part 2: Ashern to Ashern}}</ref> Lepi were prone to wild gesticulations when talking amongst themselves.<ref name="Sc">''[[Scoundrels]]''</ref>

Lepi names were typically one word, with examples including Augdon, Gagen, Javilla, Lupher, Maximort, Nevlin, Roonis, Saper, Zylo,<ref name="UAA" /> and Trixx.<ref name="GMR" />

==History==
{{Quote|Like my mother told all eighty of us kids&mdash;it'd never work out. Marry a nice girl from a nice burrow&hellip;|Jaxxon|<ref name="M10" />}}
The Lepus carnivorus evolved on the planet [[Coachelle Prime/Legends|Coachelle Prime]],<ref name="GMR" /> located in the [[Terr'skiar sector/Legends|Terr'skiar sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="SWATEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> The world was shrouded by streamers of gas from the [[Thornhedge Nebula/Legends|Thornhedge Nebula]],<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and formed part of a [[Constellation/Legends|constellation]] known on [[Oseon 6845]]<ref name="LC2">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]''</ref> as the [[Silly Rabbit]]. Due to their high reproductive rate, they soon filled their world to capacity and were driven to develop stardrives in order to avoid overcrowding. They swiftly colonized all five planets in the [[Coachelle system/Legends|Coachelle system]], along with its [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belt]]. That seemingly provided enough room for their species,<ref name="GMR" /> although some Lepi were involved in other colonization efforts such as on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="TM" /> The many [[Colony ship/Legends|colony ships]] used in these endeavors were later left largely intact and poorly guarded, susceptible to theft by enterprising Lepi, such as [[Jaxxon/Legends|Jaxxon]].<ref name="GMR" />

Coachelle became a minor trade world, located at the end of the [[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|Ootmian Pabol]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]], and connected to [[Terr'skiar]], the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The [[Droid/Legends|droid]]-manufacturing company [[Coachelle Automata/Legends|Coachelle Automata]] shared its name with the Lepi homeworld. The company produced the [[LEP servant droid/Legends|LEP servant droid]], which was in common use during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. That droid model had distinctive "ears," reminiscent of the Lepi species.<ref name="SWVGUB">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Visual Guide: Ultimate Battles]]''</ref>

==Lepi in the galaxy==
[[File:Lepi_-_Rookies.jpg|thumb|left|A Lepi in the Power Dive on Ord Mantell]]
{{Quote|Curse you Boba Fett! Damn you for tracking me to my warren and family and dragging me to Hutt "justice"!|Grubbat Fhilch|<ref name="Fortune" />}}
The Coachelle system had long provided sufficient living space for the whole of Lepus carnivorus civilization.<ref name="UAA" /> Despite that, Lepi were known offworld both by reputation<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> and via their presence there.<ref name="UAA" /> For instance, during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Galactic Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], a dance known as the [[Lepi Hop]] was known throughout the galaxy.<ref name="SWTOR" /> Further, a number of Lepi personally ventured beyond their [[Star system/Legends|star system]] into the galaxy at large. They tended to stick to the fringe as [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] and [[tech specialist]]s, while some of the more aggressive became [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]]. Some Lepi were known to have the capacity to become [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], although none were known to have achieved that feat.<ref name="UAA" /> One Lepi to leave the Coachelle system was [[Heff (Lepi)|Heff]], who was part of colonization efforts of the planet Tatooine during the early period of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Heff established a gift shop called [[Heff's Souvenirs]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] and lived to be one of the last three surviving members of the colony. He had at least one daughter, [[Tebbi]]. However, Heff was killed in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] by the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jodo Kast]], who was hunting the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon]].<ref name="TM" /> Heff's daughter later sold the shop to the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Moplin Jarron]].<ref name="GG7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

A less upright Lepi citizen was [[Grubbat Fhilch]]. He embezzled [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] from the [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] operation of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. He was subsequently tracked down to his home warren by the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], who handed him over to the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. Jabba had him thrown into a [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlacc]] pit as retribution. Fhilch was notable for possessing a long tail.<ref name="Fortune" />

Perhaps the most famous Lepus carnivorus was Jaxxon, who featured in the [[Tri-Nebula Entertainment]] [[holodocumentary]] "[[Eight for Aduba-3: The Saga of the Starhoppers]]." Originally raised on Coachelle Prime in a family of twelve siblings, he had a checkered past before his involvement in those events. After a [[Youngling/Legends|youth]] spent in juvenile centers, Jax stole a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and ventured out to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. He lived on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] for a [[Time/Legends|time]] before joining a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] group in the [[Corus system/Legends|Corus system]]. After the group was double-crossed in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], he purchased a [[WUD-500 star yacht/Legends|WUD-500 star yacht]] which he called the [[Rabbit's Foot/Legends|''Rabbit's Foot'']]. The dysfunctional ship forced him to land on Aduba-3, where he would make his claim to fame. While there, he answered a call from [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] for warriors to protect the village of [[Onacra]] against local brigands.<ref name="GMR" /> The con man [[Dozer Creed]] observed a group of Lepi engrossed in conversation on the planet [[Wukkar/Legends|Wukkar]] in 0 ABY.<ref name="Sc" />

[[File:Jaxxon-gamer.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Jaxxon, the Lepi smuggler]]
Solo assembled a group of six mercenaries for the task, in addition to himself and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] copilot [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. Wielding twin heavy [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]], Jaxxon and his companions fought strongly against [[Serji-X Arrogantus]] and his [[Cloud-Riders/Legends|Cloud-Riders]], finally repelling them with the aid of the [[Behemoth from the World Below]] which was summoned by a local [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]]. With his reward credits, the green Lepi was able to leave Aduba-3, having teamed up with the [[Human/Legends|Human]] woman [[Amaiza Foxtrain/Legends|Amaiza Foxtrain]].<ref name="M10" /><ref name="M8" /><ref name="M9">[[Star Wars (1977) 9|''Star Wars'' (1977) 9]]</ref>

The ramifications of the Aduba event did not finish there for Jaxxon, however, as he was soon attacked by the bounty hunters [[Remel Fud]] and [[Dafi (bounty hunter)|Dafi]], under orders of [[Beilert Valance/Legends|Beilert Valance]]. He was seeking one [[Jimm Doshun]] from Aduba-3, erroneously believing him to be [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. Jax was [[Torture/Legends|tortured]], but showing typical Lepi resilience, gave up little information to the hunters. However, when they later inadvertently revealed the location of Jimm, the Lepi returned to Aduba to fight off the hunters.<ref name="M16">[[Star Wars (1977) 16|''Star Wars'' (1977) 16]]</ref>

Later, in [[137 ABY]], a Lepi named [[Gusha]] owned [[Gusha's Luck]], a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on Tatooine. It was frequented by another Lepi, along with the former Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]]-turned-[[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Cade Skywalker]].<ref name="Legacy 38">[[Legacy (2006) 38|''Legacy'' (2006) 38]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Hey, I like six-foot, green carnivorous bunnies&mdash;so sue me.|[[Jeff Grubb]], author of ''[[Tempest Feud]]''|<ref name="Bunnies">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=sw20020523dchat&c=rpg|text=Hutts, New Fish, and Bunnies|date=2002-03-26}}</ref>}}
[[File:Buckyohare.jpg|thumb|left|Bucky O'Hare and his companions]]
The Lepi first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 8|''Star Wars'' (1977) 8]] published in [[February]] [[1978]], featuring Jaxxon as one of the Aduba 8. This was the first [[Marvel Comics]] story arc after the adaptation of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The species was created by writer [[Roy Thomas]] in homage to [[Wikipedia:Bugs Bunny|Bugs Bunny]], who often addressed strangers with the generic nickname "Jackson" in his 1940s cartoons.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|jaxxon|Jaxxon}}</ref> He also bore a striking resemblance to two other characters: the cartoon character [[Wikipedia:Bucky O'Hare|Bucky O'Hare]], who debuted shortly after the Marvel run, and [[Wikipedia:Jazz Jackrabbit|Jazz Jackrabbit]], a platform [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|computer]] game character. Jaxxon called himself a "Lepus carnivorus": Lepus carnivorus is [[Wikipedia:Latin language|Latin]] for "carnivorous rabbit," and the species name would later be shortened to Lepi, the Latin plural. [[Star Wars (1977) 16|''Star Wars'' (1977) 16]] misspelled the scientific name of Jaxxon's species as "Lepus carnivorous."

After his appearance in the Marvel story arc, Jaxxon was largely ignored in later [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] publications. He was brought out of limbo in the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' article ''[[The Starhoppers of Aduba-3]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]&mdash;with [[Cory J. Herndon]] and [[Michael Mikaelian]]&mdash;published [[March 1]], [[2001]]. This article gave a bio for Jaxxon as well as providing information on the species in general. Hidalgo drew inspiration from Bugs Bunny in his choice of the Coachelle system as their star system. In the 1953 short "[[Wikipedia:Bully for Bugs|Bully for Bugs]]," Bugs asks, "Excuse me, can you direct me to the Coachella Valley and the Giant Carrot Festival&hellip; therein?" Hidalgo carefully mirrored this sentence, also ending his in "therein."<ref name="Endnotes">{{Blog|pablog|60|Tales of the Big Green Bunny: Behind the Scenes of Gamer #4 &mdash; The Coachella Valley, and the Giant Carrot Festival}}</ref>

[[File:Max.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Max, in [[Barons Hed]]]]
Through providing example names for Lepi, the ''Starhoppers'' article [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] several rabbit-like individuals as Lepus carnivorus. These included Heff&mdash;and by proxy, Tebbi&mdash;from ''[[Tatooine Manhunt]]'' ([[June]] [[1988]]) and Grubbat Fhilch from the '' [[Star Wars Tales]]'' comic "[[Fortune, Fate, and the Natural History of the Sarlacc]]" ([[December 20]], [[2000]]). It also gave "Trixx" as a common Lepi name. This is a reference to the cereal [[Wikipedia:Trix (cereal)|Trix]], whose advertisements feature a rabbit who tries to trick kids into giving him the fruit-flavored food before being told, "Silly rabbit, Trix are for kids." The name was not in Hidalgo's original submission, but was changed in editing.<ref name="Endnotes" /> The Silly Rabbit constellation is also a reference to these Trix ads.

The Lepi were also featured in the ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' ([[April 19]], [[2003]]), which provided further example Lepi names. Among these was Maximort, which suggests a connection with the rabbit-like character [[Max (bunny)|Max]], previously [[canon]]ized by [[Abel G. Peña]] in ''[[The Dark Forces Saga]]'' ([[April 7]], [[2005]]). Max appeared as an unlockable cameo in ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' ([[October 9]], [[1997]]).

Since this time, Lepi have appeared in a couple of other sources. Jaxxon made it into [[July]] [[2005]]'s [[Star Wars Insider 83|''Star Wars Insider'' 83]], in the ''[[20 Most Memorable Moments of the Expanded Universe]]'', where he was cited as one of the five goofiest moments.
